raft_ocean.story.log.0:
GLASSWATCH — Mara, lookout keeper

For nine nights I counted a light beyond the rain. Ivo said it was lightning. On the tenth night it answered: three flashes, a pause, three more. Someone was still out there. We spread the charts across the lookout table and marked every answer, even the faint ones.

Then our fresh water ran low. Ivo wanted to take the receiver aboard and leave. Sela asked for two more days; her seedlings had roots now. I stayed at the ladder until morning, listening to an empty channel. There is a difference between silence and nobody listening. I am trying to remember it.

NEXT: Find Garden Relay and Sela's journal. If its glasshouse has survived, take seeds, but leave enough for another boat.
raft_ocean.story.log.1:
GARDEN RELAY — Sela, seed keeper

The first green shoot came up in a cracked cup. Mara brought it to me as if it were a rescued passenger. Now there are rows under glass, rain in the cauldron and three names scratched into my potting bench. Ivo patched the roof even while arguing that we should abandon it.

The storm took the relay mast, not the garden. Before we left, I packed our route charts into Echo Vault. The key is here because somebody returning hungry should be able to find us. The switches remember our watch: Mara awake, the empty middle bunk, Ivo awake. LEFT ON, MIDDLE OFF, RIGHT ON. Use the relay key on the seal.

NEXT: Find Echo Vault. Its charts tell you where the last guiding light stood.
raft_ocean.story.log.2:
ECHO VAULT — Ivo, chart maker

I built this room to keep our maps dry. Then I caught myself locking it as if ink belonged to me. Mara asked what a safe route was worth if nobody could read it. We put shelves along the walls and made copies until our hands shook.

The northern passage was my mistake. I trusted a shoreline that had moved after the storm. A supply boat following my chart never reached our harbor. I crossed the route out, but Mara kept its last bearing: Ember Beacon. She would not let one bad chart become an excuse to stop answering.

NEXT: Sail to Ember Beacon and climb to the lantern room. The keeper's journal may tell us whether that boat reached land.

raft_ocean.story.log.3:
EMBER BEACON — Mara, last lighthouse watch

The boat arrived with its sail wrapped around the mast. Two passengers, an empty tank and Sela's seed tin lashed under a bench. Ivo's route had led them through the wrong channel, but the beacon brought them the rest of the way. We gave them the keeper's cottage. Nobody slept that first night.

Ivo wanted to shut down the light and save the copper for our engine. Then he climbed the ladder carrying a new coil. He never apologized in words. The lantern burned until sunrise. We left the cottage stocked and took the rescued crew to Tideworks Haven.

NEXT: Follow the signal to Tideworks Haven. Our departure plan is in the harbor workshop journal, beside the repaired tanks.
raft_ocean.story.log.4:
TIDEWORKS HAVEN — Sela, departure morning

The pier was too narrow for everyone, so Ivo extended it. The workshop smelled of wet timber and hot iron. Mara hung lamps along the posts so the passengers could board before dawn. Our little argument about one cup of water had somehow become a boat full of people.

We are leaving together. Not because these islands are useless, but because we can carry what we learned to the next coast. The harbor key opens Starfall Archive, where we stored the corrected charts. Facing its seal: LEFT ON, MIDDLE OFF, RIGHT ON. Use the key; keep the charts.

NEXT: Visit Starfall Archive and the observatory beside it. Our latest copied entry is there. If another crew arrives late, the seeds and repair benches are for them.
raft_ocean.story.log.5:
STARFALL ARCHIVE — An unfinished transmission

MARA: We thought the lights were scattered survivors. From the observatory we saw a chain. Then, beyond its last light, the receiver caught a different rhythm. A voice said 'bring the ledger' before the storm swallowed the rest. Nobody here knew that call. It answered again after we had switched our own beacon off.

IVO: I corrected the northern chart, but this signal belongs to no route we recorded. Its bearing wandered east whenever the clouds closed in. I will not mark another guessed harbor as safe. We need a clearer transmission before these charts can lead anyone farther. The missing words may matter more than the bearing.

SELA: We left this copy in the archive and took the seed tins aboard. Mara is keeping watch; Ivo is listening. We are sailing east together, but we do not yet know who is calling, or what ledger they expect us to carry. If we learn more, we will leave another entry where the next crew can find it. Until then, the channel remains open.
